newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia bars Megawati backers from poll rallies.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia bars Megawati backers from poll rallies.

text.p: Indonesia will not allow supporters of ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri to stage rallies during the official election campaign, the official Antara news agency reported on Thursday.

Interior Ministry spokesman H.S.A. Yusacc was quoted as saying that Megawati's supporters within the split Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) would be denied permission to stage their own campaign if they requested it.

"The government's stand has since the beginning been clear, namely to uphold the principle of legality that only the PDI under the leadership elected at the Medan congress will be permitted to organise election campaigns," Yusacc said.

The government funded the Medan congress in June at which Megawati was ousted by deputy parliamentary speaker Surjadi, in a move which political analysts said was supported by authorities because they feared she was becoming too popular.

Megawati and her backers, who boycotted the congress, have refused to recognise its results, saying it was illegal under the party's statutes. A legal challenge to the congress is before the High Court.
Last month, the General Election Institute approved a list of Surjadi's candidates that excluded all known supporters of Megawati from the May 29 general election.

On Thursday, about 100 Megawati supporters staged a peaceful protest in front of the office of the coordinating minister of politics and security affairs in central Jakarta, asking the government to allow Megawati to join the election.
"There is no reason to say the PDI under Megawati Sukarnoputri is not ready to join the general elections," a statement prepared by the protesters, who were mostly students, said.

On Tuesday, thousands of Megawati supporters took to the streets in parades and convoys in a number of cities on the main island of Java, including the capital Jakarta, to protest against the election body's rejection of her candidates.
In December, the government said it feared outbreaks of violence and it issued regulations banning street protests during the official election campaign period, which begins on April 29.

Only the ruling Golkar, Christian-Nationalist PDI and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party are allowed to contest the election. All candidates of three parties must be approved by a government body which includes military members.
